newsitem.title: FINLAND: RAUTARUUKKI SEES END-97 STEEL PRICES UP.
newsitem.headline: RAUTARUUKKI SEES END-97 STEEL PRICES UP.

text.p: Finnish steel group Rautaruukki Oy expects steel prices to rise by 10 percent this year on end-1996 prices but to show no change on average over 1996, the group's CEO said on Wednesday.

"We expect prices of both flat and long steel products to be about 10 percent higher at the end of the year than they were at the when the year began," Rautaruukki CEO Mikko Kivimaki told a briefing on the group's January-April results.
"This year's prices will, on average, be at the same level as last year," Kivimaki said.

Rautaruukki reported January-April profits before extraordinaries and tax down 20 percent to 285 million markka from 357 million a year ago, and it attributed the decline to lower prices during the review period.
But Kivimaki said prices have now headed upward.

"This year's price profile will be approximately a mirror image of last year's," Kivimaki said. "Last year the best prices were at the beginning of the year, and this year the best prices will be at the end of the year."
"The profit for the whole of 1997 should be better than that for 1996 provided that steel markets develop as forecast," Rautaruukki said in a statement with its results.
In 1996, Rautaruukki had pre-tax profits before extraordinary items of 715 million markka.

The improving price prospects, expected higher demand in Europe and continued strong demand in the United States and the Far East would help Rautaruukki improve upon its 1996 result, the company said in the interim report.
In the four-months to end-April, average markka-denominated prices of Rautaruukki's deliveries of flat and tubular steel products were down eight percent on the year-ago level, it said.
Average Swedish crown-denominated prices of the long steel products made by its Fundia unit were meanwhile down six percent, Rautaruukki said.

In January-April, Fundia's operating profit fell 59 percent to 15 million markka, but Kivimaki said that, while the unit's first tertial result was down on the same period last year, it was better than the result for the second or third tertials.
"That means Fundia's earnings trend has clearly turned upward," he said.

Also reporting four-month results on Wednesday, Finnish engineering group Metra said demand for the special steels produced by its Imatra Steel unit had risen, and that it expected prices to rise in the second half of the year.
